fact_en: A large industrial electromagnet in a scrap yard generates enough magnetic force to lift an entire crushed car weighing over 1,500 kilograms!
fact_bis: Ang dako nga industrial electromagnet sa scrap yard makapahimo og igong magnetic force aron buhian ang tibuok nga gisi nga sakyanan nga nagtimbang og sobra 1,500 kilograms!

findings.note: EN: electromagnet 'generates enough magnetic force to LIFT an entire crushed car (1,500 kg)'. BIS: 'makapahimo og igong magnetic force aron BUHIAN ang tibuok nga gisi nga sakyanan' — buhian = to RELEASE / let go, the opposite of alsahon (lift). The card's whole point (a magnet can pick up a 1,500 kg car) is reversed into the magnet letting the car go, and nothing else in the card supplies 'lift'.

fact_en:
Does a loud shout travel faster than a quiet whisper?

Nope! In the same air, both travel at the exact same speed of about 343 meters per second.
fact_bis:
Mas paspas ba ang kusog nga singgit kaysa sa hilum nga hunong?

Dili! Sa parehas nga hangin, pareho ra ang ilang bilis nga mga 343 metros kada segundo!

findings.note: EN: 'Does a loud shout travel faster than a quiet WHISPER?' BIS: 'kusog nga singgit kaysa sa hilum nga HUNONG?' — hunong = to STOP/halt; whisper is hunghong. The second item of the comparison stops being a sound at all, so the card's point (loudness does not change sound speed) is unanswerable from the Cebuano; the body never repeats the correct word.

fact_en: Giant electromagnets powered by electricity in Quezon City scrap yards temporarily attract and lift heavy pieces of discarded iron and steel!
fact_bis: Dagkong electromagnets nga gipadagan sa kuryente sa mga scrap yard sa Quezon City temporaryong makaakit ug makabug-at og discarded iron ug steel!

findings.note: EN: scrap-yard electromagnets 'temporarily attract and LIFT heavy pieces of discarded iron and steel'. BIS: 'temporaryong makaakit ug MAKABUG-AT og discarded iron ug steel' — makabug-at = can MAKE HEAVY, not makaalsa (can lift). As written the card asserts that magnets make scrap iron heavy, and the lifting fact is gone from the card.

fact_en: Ice has a friction coefficient of about 0.03, making it roughly 25 times slipperier than rubber on dry asphalt, which is 0.8!
fact_bis: Ang yelo adunay friction coefficient nga mga 0.03, mao nga mga 25 ka beses mas slippery kaysa goma sa uga nga asphalt nga 0.8!

findings.note: title_bis 'Malisod nga Yelo' for title_en 'Slippery Ice'. Malisod = DIFFICULT (lisod); slippery is madanlog/madanglog. The title names a different property than the card teaches, and the body uses the correct sense (the English loan 'mas slippery kaysa goma'), marking the title as the outlier.

fact_en:
How can we see an apple if it doesn't make its own light?

We see it because ambient light reflects off its surface and enters our eyes!
fact_bis:
Unsaon nato pagkakita sa mansanas kung dili kini mohatag og kaugalingong suga?

Makita nato kini kay ang ambient light nag-reflect sa iyang nawong ug mosulod sa atong mga mata!

findings.note: title_bis 'Pamalandong' for title_en 'Reflection'. Pamalandong is mental reflection / contemplation (palandong = to ponder); optical reflection is repleksyon / pagsalamin. The title names a completely different thing — and the card's own body uses the correct sense ('ang ambient light NAG-REFLECT sa iyang nawong'), which is the evidence the title is the outlier. This is the English-homonym trap, not compact title style.

fact_en: When two mirrors face each other, light bounces back and forth between them, creating many repeating images!
fact_bis: Kon mag-atubang ang duha ka salamin, ang kahayag mobalik-balik tali kanila, busa daghan ug sunod-sunod nga hulagway ang makita!

findings.note: Same defect as ffct-27757: title_bis 'Pamalandong' for title_en 'Mirror Reflection'. Pamalandong = meditation/contemplation, never optical reflection (repleksyon / pagsalamin sa samin). Here the body never supplies the correct word either — it only describes light bouncing ('ang kahayag mobalik-balik tali kanila') — so the Cebuano title label for mirror reflection is simply wrong.

fact_en: Holding a hot piece of volcanic pumice rock warms your hands through direct heat conduction!
fact_bis: Kung imong hawakan ang init nga volcanic pumice rock, mokusog ang imong mga kamot pinaagi sa direct heat conduction!

findings.note: EN: holding hot pumice 'WARMS your hands through direct heat conduction'. BIS: 'mokusog ang imong mga kamot' = your hands become STRONG (kusog = strength), not moinit/mopainit (become warm). A child reads that holding a hot rock makes your hands strong — a false claim, and the actual fact (heat transfers into your hands) is never stated anywhere on the card.

fact_en:
How do tiny insects climb a narra tree without slipping?

The rough bark of a narra tree increases friction, allowing small insects to climb the trunk without slipping!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pag-akyat ang gagmay nga insekto sa narra tree nga dili madulas?

Ang garbong kahoy sa narra tree nagdugang friction, mao nga ang gagmay nga insekto makakapyot sa kahoy nga dili madulas!

findings.note: EN: "The ROUGH BARK of a narra tree increases friction". BIS: "Ang garbong kahoy sa narra tree nagdugang friction" — garbo in Cebuano = PRIDE / elegance / flair, so this reads "the elegant wood of the narra". Two losses that are never restored: the mechanism (surface roughness is why friction is high — the only science the card carries) and panit/bark becomes kahoy/wood. A child reading only the Cebuano cannot answer "why don't the insects slip?" with anything but "because narra wood". Correct word is magaspang, which this very batch uses properly in ffct-27872.

fact_en: Rough abaca ropes have high friction! This stops them from slipping when Filipino fishermen tie their small bangka boats to wooden docks.
fact_bis: Ang magaspang nga abaca ropes adunay high friction! Mao nga dili sila maluspad kung ang mga mangingisda magtali sa ilang gagmay nga bangka sa kahoy nga pier.

findings.note: EN: rough abaca rope's high friction "stops them from slipping" when fishermen tie bangka to docks. BIS: "Mao nga dili sila maluspad kung ang mga mangingisda magtali..." — luspad = PALE / FADED, not slip (danlog / madulas / madalin-as). The Cebuano therefore teaches that high friction keeps the rope from fading in colour, which is false, and the slipping fact — the whole point of the card — appears nowhere else in the card. Same-batch evidence that the corpus knows the right word: ffct-27821, ffct-27885, ffct-27893 and ffct-27902 all use madulas/pagdulas/danlog correctly for slipping; this card's own body already uses magaspang correctly for 'rough', so maluspad is the lone outlier.

fact_en:
How does a bunot clean Filipino wooden floors?

The rough texture of a dried coconut husk (bunot) increases friction, making it perfect for scrubbing dirt off traditional wooden floors!
fact_bis:
Unsaon paglimpyo sa bunot sa kahoy nga salog sa mga Pilipino?

Ang garbong texture sa uga nga panit sa lubi (bunot) nagdugang og friction, maayo kaayo ni pangtangtang og hugaw sa tradisyonal nga kahoy nga salog!

findings.note: Same swap as ffct-27821: EN "The ROUGH TEXTURE of a dried coconut husk (bunot) increases friction" → BIS "Ang garbong texture sa uga nga panit sa lubi (bunot) nagdugang og friction", i.e. "the elegant/proud texture". Nothing in the card restores 'rough' in Cebuano, so the reason bunot grips and scrubs is gone. Flagged with slightly lower confidence than ffct-27821 because 'texture ... nagdugang og friction' still gets the child partway to the answer — but the wrong word is the same real Cebuano word meaning something else, and the fix is the same (magaspang).

fact_en:
Why are capiz shells perfect for parol lanterns?

Because their smooth, polished surfaces reflect light brightly, making your traditional Filipino lanterns shine beautifully!
fact_bis:
Ngano nga perfect ang capiz shells para sa mga parol?

Tungod sa hamis ug hayag nilang ibabaw, nag-reflect sila og kusog nga kahayag para sa nindot nga mga parol!

findings.note: title_bis "Pamalandong" for title_en "Light Reflection". Palandong/pamalandong in Cebuano = MEDITATION, pondering, contemplation — the mental sense of English "reflection", never the optical one (pagsalamin / banaag / 'reflection'). A child sees a card titled "Meditation" over a card about capiz shells bouncing light. The body never repairs it in Cebuano: it only says "nag-reflect sila og kusog nga kahayag", i.e. the English loanword, so the wrong Cebuano sense is never corrected.

fact_en: Because sound needs a physical medium like air or water to travel, outer space is completely silent.
fact_bis: Kay ang tingog nanginahanglan og physical medium sama sa air o tubig aron makalakaw, ang outer space hingpit nga hilum.

findings.note: title_bis "Hilom nga Kahangturan" for title_en "Silent Outer Space". Kahangturan = ETERNITY / forever (time), not outer space (kawanangan / kalawakan). The title names a different thing and the body only uses the English "outer space", so no Cebuano word ever restores it. Same batch proves the correct word is available: ffct-27810 is titled "Tunog sa Kawanangan" for "Sound in Space".
